entity_ranked_evidence.title: Delhi logs 648 fresh COVID cases, 5 fatalities
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: ## New Delhi [India], July 3 (ANI): Delhi reported 648 new COVID-19 cases and five deaths in the last 24 hours, as per the Delhi government’s health bulletin on Sunday. The active cases stand in the city at 3,268 with a daily positivity rate of 4.29 per cent. As many as 785 COVID patients recovered in the last 24 hours, taking the total number of recoveries from the disease since the beginning of the pandemic to 19,07,474. Meanwhile, India reported 16,103 new COVID cases in the last 24 hours with a daily case positivity rate of 4.27 per cent, as per the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on Sunday. According to the Ministry, 13,929 COVID patients recovered from the disease in the last 24 hours taking the total number of recoveries in the country to 4,28,65,519. As many as 31 patients succumbed to the virus in the last 24 hours, taking the death toll to 5,25,199.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Coronavirus Deaths: At 24 in a week, Delhi logs India's highest Covid deaths | India News - Times of India
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: During this period (April 9-15), neighbouring Haryana registered 4,554 fresh cases, the fourth highest in the country, followed at number 5 by Uttar Pradesh with 3,332. Rajasthan, with a four-fold rise in cases, reported 14 fatalities from the virus, the third highest during the week after Delhi and Maharashtra (19).Read Less. In the last seven days, Delhi reported 24 deaths linked to Covid, the highest in the country and logged the second highest number of cases at 7,664. (With Sunday's data from Delhi coming in, the seven-day count of cases in the capital has risen to 8,599 and the seven-day toll stands at 23.). Rajasthan, with a four-fold rise in cases, reported 14 fatalities from the virus, the third highest during the week after Delhi and Maharashtra (19). Meanwhile, the number of states reporting over 2,000 fresh cases in the past seven days has risen to 10, up from four in the preceding week.
